title: The Side Project Andrew Mason Started to Find a Business Model
conflicts: The Point's seed money: TechCrunch (2008) reported $2.5 million from angels; Mason (Mixergy, 2010) said Lefkofsky's investment was $1 million. The story gives both. First deal: AP (2009) says $20 of pizza for $10 to fewer than two dozen people; secondary accounts call it two-for-one or half price at Motel Bar; the story uses AP and does not name the bar. Who drove the pivot: Mason's S-1 letter says Lefkofsky kept 'bugging' him for a business model; a University of Michigan alumni piece says Mason approached Lefkofsky; the story follows Mason.
notes: Main primary sources: Mason's 2011 S-1 founder letter (reproduced in full by TechCrunch) and his 2010 Mixergy interview. Mason's 'totally ghetto' description of the first version is not quoted; 'so cobbled together' is used instead. Stance 'complicates': the Dhammapada verse prizes the single clear word, as Mason prized one deal a day, but judges it by whether it brings quiet.
